title: 32yo M Tension Pneumothorax
chiefComplaint: Chest pain and severe dyspnoea after a motorcycle crash
background: Motorcycle versus pickup truck at about 60 km/h, 25 minutes ago. He was wearing a helmet, no loss of consciousness. He landed on his left side against a kerb. EMS report progressive dyspnoea and falling saturations during transport despite a non-rebreather mask. No past medical history, no medications, does not smoke.

exam.finding: Agitated, air hungry, unable to lie flat, diaphoretic, in obvious distress
Trachea deviated to the right at the suprasternal notch, distended neck veins, helmet abrasion over left zygoma, no midface instability, cervical collar in place
Sinus tachycardia, heart sounds displaced to the right and distant, radial pulse thready and absent on inspiration, capillary refill 5 seconds
Absent breath sounds over the entire left hemithorax, hyperresonant to percussion on the left, left chest wall lagging on inspiration, tenderness and crepitus over left ribs 4 to 7
Soft, mildly tender in the left upper quadrant, no rebound or guarding, pelvis stable, no seatbelt sign
Cool, pale and mottled peripheries, subcutaneous emphysema over the left chest wall and supraclavicular fossa, road rash over left shoulder and hip, no external haemorrhage
GCS 13 (E3V4M6), restless and confused from hypoxia, pupils 3 mm equal and reactive, moves all four limbs

investigations.name: eFAST (bedside ultrasound)
investigations.report: Left anterior chest: absent lung sliding, absent B-lines, barcode sign on M-mode with a lung point laterally. No pericardial effusion. No free fluid in Morison's pouch, splenorenal recess or pelvis. Performed in 90 seconds at the bedside without delaying decompression.

investigations.name: Portable Chest X-ray (post decompression)
investigations.report: Left chest drain in situ with tip directed apically. Residual 10% left apical pneumothorax. Left ribs 5 and 6 fractures. Mediastinum midline. No haemothorax. Lungs otherwise clear.

investigations.name: Arterial blood gas (on 15 L/min)
investigations.report: Mixed respiratory and metabolic acidosis with severe hypoxaemia. Drawn before decompression.

investigations.name: Lactate
investigations.report: Obstructive shock with impaired venous return.

investigations.name: Haemoglobin
investigations.report: Near normal. Argues against major haemorrhage as the dominant cause of shock, though early haemoglobin can be falsely reassuring.

investigations.name: 12-Lead ECG
investigations.report: Sinus tachycardia at 132/min. Low voltage complexes in the left precordial leads. No electrical alternans. No ischaemic changes.

investigations.name: Group and crossmatch
investigations.report: Two units crossmatched and held. Massive transfusion protocol not activated.

data.label: Primary survey with high flow oxygen and cervical spine control
Explain the needle decompression to him before you do it and get verbal consent (Empathy)
data.narrative: He is frightened and fighting the mask. You name what you are about to do and why, in one sentence, and put a hand on his shoulder. He stops fighting and lets you work. Nurse Ann notes you did not have to sedate him.

data.label: Immediate needle or finger decompression, do not wait for the X-ray
actions: Needle thoracostomy, 5th intercostal space anterior axillary line, left

doseMap.Needle thoracostomy, 5th intercostal spa: 14G cannula at least 5 cm long, or open finger thoracostomy if body habitus is thick

data.label: Immediate response
data.narrative: A rush of air escapes. The trachea returns to midline within a minute, neck veins flatten, and his agitation settles as saturations climb.

doseMap.Tube thoracostomy, left, 5th intercostal: 28 Fr drain to underwater seal, no clamping

data.label: IV access, analgesia and confirmatory chest X-ray

doseMap.Fentanyl IV titrated: 25-50 mcg IV every 5 min to effect, monitor respiratory rate

data.label: Stabilised
data.narrative: The drain swings and bubbles on expiration. Repeat film shows the lung nearly fully re-expanded. He is pain free enough to take deep breaths.

data.label: Complete secondary survey and trauma imaging
actions: CT chest, abdomen and pelvis with contrast

data.label: Disposition
data.narrative: CT confirms left rib fractures 4 to 7 with a small pulmonary contusion and no intra-abdominal injury. He is admitted to the surgical ward with the drain, incentive spirometry and a regional block plan.
